title: Markdown that reports need

steps.say: ## starts a section, and the contents list picks it up. **bold** and *italic* mark the words that matter.
A list written straight under a line of text does not become a list. Markdown reads it as more of the same paragraph.
The fix is one blank line before the list. Most Markdown surprises are a missing blank line.
A link is [text](address). A footnote is [^1] in the text and a [^1]: line anywhere; Quarto numbers it and moves it to the end.
Math goes between $ signs in a sentence, or $$ on lines of its own. A methods note can be exact.
One catch: MathJax draws the formula, fetched from the internet when the page opens. html-math-method: mathml writes it into the page, so it shows offline.

---
title: "Unemployment in the regions"
subtitle: "Synthetic data, for training only"
author: "Labour statistics team"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
    html-math-method: mathml
---

## Summary

Unemployment **fell** in most regions between 2022 and 2025.
*Jazan* is the exception. This note shows the national
trend and the latest rates.[^1]
The data cover:

- 13 regions and the Kingdom as a whole
- 16 quarters, from 2022 Q1 to 2025 Q4

Official figures are on the [GASTAT website](https://www.stats.gov.sa).

[^1]: All figures in this note are synthetic, made for training.

## Method

The unemployment rate is

$$
u = \frac{U}{U + E} \times 100
$$

where $U$ is the number unemployed and $E$ the number employed.

## Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
glimpse(rates)
```

## Trend

```{r}
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
ggplot(kingdom, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```
